corrections.before: A visible opening into the peritoneal space is a wall breach. Its small size, clean field, mobile margins and prompt recognition support endoscopic clipping. Stable vital signs do not establish that an open defect is sealed. Supportive treatment, hospital monitoring and surgical involvement remain necessary. An apposed clip line does not prevent gas already outside the bowel from creating pressure. The new abdominal, ventilatory and circulatory changes require emergency percutaneous decompression while resuscitation and hospital escalation continue. This is temporization; improvement does not prove that the injury is sealed.
corrections.after: A visible opening into the peritoneal space is a wall breach. Its small size, clean field, mobile margins and prompt recognition support endoscopic clipping. Stable vital signs do not establish that an open defect is sealed. Supportive treatment, hospital monitoring and surgical involvement remain necessary. Gas that escaped before insufflation stopped can remain outside the bowel after clip apposition. Here, abdominal expansion is evolving during the final closure steps and produces a new combined ventilatory and circulatory problem at reassessment. Emergency percutaneous decompression precedes transfer while airway and circulatory support continue. Improvement is temporization and does not establish a durable seal or remove the need for hospital assessment.
